title: Miketz: it is not in me (Genesis 41:16)
hook: Joseph tells Pharaoh the meaning comes from God, not from him

segments.voice: Yesterday, Miketz: two full years of waiting, then out of the dungeon in a day. Your line was it ends suddenly. Today, Joseph stands before Pharaoh.

You finally get the meeting with the big boss. Or the audition, or the chance to pitch the idea to the person who can make it happen. And they say: I hear you're the one who can do this. The easy reply is: yes, that's me. Joseph has just been pulled out of the dungeon, shaved and changed. He's standing in Pharaoh's court, a prisoner one hour ago. Pharaoh says: I've had a dream, and I've heard that you can read dreams.
screen: `THE BIG MEETING.` → `I HEAR YOU'RE THE ONE.` → `A PRISONER BEFORE PHARAOH.`

segments.voice: Joseph's first words to Pharaoh, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace." In Hebrew, the first part is a single word, biladai. Not me. Apart from me. Think about the risk. Joseph needs Pharaoh to think he's valuable; he has one shot to get out of prison for good. And the first thing he does is hand the credit away. Remember the young Joseph, seventeen, telling his brothers about dreams where their sheaves bowed down to his? That Joseph talked a lot about himself. This one, after the pit and the prison, talks about God. And he keeps doing it. Pharaoh tells both dreams, the cows and the ears of grain, and Joseph says: God has told Pharaoh what he is about to do. Seven years of plenty, seven years of famine. The dream came twice because the thing is fixed by God, and God will do it soon. Again and again, Joseph names God. Here's the surprise: giving the credit away doesn't make him smaller. Pharaoh looks around his court and asks: could we find anyone like this, a man with the spirit of God in him? And he puts Joseph over all of Egypt. The rabbis prized this. The Mishnah says that whoever repeats a teaching in the name of the one who said it brings redemption into the world. The lesson they drew is plain: say where things came from.
screen: `BILADAI: NOT ME.` · `THE BOY WHO TALKED ABOUT HIMSELF.` · `GOD HAS TOLD PHARAOH.` · `SAY IT IN THE NAME OF WHO SAID IT.` · then, large: `IT IS NOT IN ME.`

segments.voice: Think of something you're proud of lately: a good result at work, a meal, a kid who's doing well, a hard day you got through. Trace it back: who taught you, who helped, what was given to you that you didn't make yourself? If you pray, you can thank God for it; either way, choose one person you could name out loud.
Miketz. At the end: the portion where Joseph, before Pharaoh, says the meaning isn't in him, but comes from God.
Your line: not in me. In his one big chance, Joseph's first word pointed past himself. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jewish learning takes care to cite who said what, and students repeat teachings in the name of the teacher who first taught them, following the Mishnah's saying about bringing redemption.

chat.says: Joseph finally gets his big chance with Pharaoh and says, it is not in me. Why?
options: He gave the credit to God, and Pharaoh trusted him more for it, not less.
He was afraid of failing, so he lowered Pharaoh's hopes on purpose.
He meant another prisoner was the real reader of dreams.
chat.meaning: Biladai: not me. Joseph named God again and again, and Pharaoh set him over Egypt. The rabbis prized saying where things came from.
